{{short description|Family of groups in group theory}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:<sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub> (mathematics)}}
In mathematics, '''<sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub>''' is a family of [[Steinberg group (Lie theory)|Steinberg]] or twisted [[Chevalley group]]s. It is a quasi-split form of [[E6 (mathematics)|E<sub>6</sub>]], depending on a quadratic extension of fields ''K''&sub;''L''. Unfortunately the notation for the group is not standardized, as some authors write it as <sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub>(''K'') (thinking of <sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub> as an [[algebraic group]] taking values in ''K'') and some as <sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub>(''L'') (thinking of the group as a subgroup of E<sub>6</sub>(''L'') fixed by an outer involution).

Over [[finite field]]s these groups form one of the 18 infinite families of [[finite simple group]]s, and were introduced independently by {{harvtxt|Tits|1958}} and {{harvtxt|Steinberg|1959}}.

==Over finite fields==

The group <sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub>(''q''<sup>2</sup>) has order
''q''<sup>36</sup>
(''q''<sup>12</sup>&nbsp;−&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>9</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>8</sup>&nbsp;−&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>6</sup>&nbsp;−&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>5</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;−&nbsp;1)
/(3,''q''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1).<ref>Reading example: If ''q''<sup>2</sup>=2<sup>2</sup> in <sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub>(''q''<sup>2</sup>) then ''q''=2 in the order formula ''q''<sup>36</sup>
(''q''<sup>12</sup>&nbsp;−&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>9</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>8</sup>&nbsp;−&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>6</sup>&nbsp;−&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>5</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)
(''q''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;−&nbsp;1)
/(3,''q''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1). However, the group <sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub>(2<sup>2</sup>) is sometimes also written <sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub>(2) (e.&nbsp;g. in [[#Wilson|Wilson's Atlas]]).</ref>
This is similar to the order ''q''<sup>36</sup>
(''q''<sup>12</sup> − 1)
(''q''<sup>9</sup> − 1)
(''q''<sup>8</sup> − 1)
(''q''<sup>6</sup> − 1)
(''q''<sup>5</sup> − 1)
(''q''<sup>2</sup> − 1)
/(3,''q'' − 1)
of E<sub>6</sub>(''q'').

Its Schur multiplier has order (3, ''q''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1) except for ''q''=2, i.&nbsp;e. <sup>2</sup>''E''<sub>6</sub>(2<sup>2</sup>), when it has order 12  and is a product of cyclic groups of orders 2,2,3. One of the exceptional double covers of <sup>2</sup>''E''<sub>6</sub>(2<sup>2</sup>) is a subgroup of the baby monster group,
and the exceptional central extension by the elementary abelian group of order 4 is a subgroup of the monster group.

The outer  automorphism group has order (3,&nbsp;''q''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)&nbsp;·&nbsp;''f'' where ''q''<sup>2</sup> =&nbsp;''p''<sup>''f''</sup>.

==Over the real numbers==

Over the real numbers, <sup>2</sup>E<sub>6</sub> is the quasisplit form of E<sub>6</sub>, and is one of the five real forms of E<sub>6</sub> classified by [[Élie Cartan]]. Its maximal compact subgroup is of type&nbsp;[[F4 (mathematics)|F<sub>4</sub>]].
